subject: A priori power analysis for regression using simsem

messages.author: 556685e17a412579
messages.subject: A priori power analysis for regression using simsem
parts:
Hi!

I have been using the simsem tutorial (https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-022-01996-0), to write some simulations for my experiments.

In one case, I needed to write the same code for a regression with one dummy variable as predictor. The problem was that I did not have endogenous variables, beyond the dependent variable. Thus, the code did not function (see the code 1 below), and I tried code 2 but again with problems, i mention below:

Code 1

#########
designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = 1:0)
exodata <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:100, function(i) designMatrix))
a.Int <- 0.4
#------------------------------  
#Exogenous Paths
 
  kappa.free <- kappa.pop <- matrix(0,
                                    nrow = 1, # each row is one endogenous outcome: Y
                                    ncol = 1, # each column is one exogenous predictor: X
                                    dimnames = list(c("X", "Y"),names(exodata)))
  kappa.free["Y","X"] <- "a.Int"
  kappa.pop["Y","X"] <- a.Int
  (exoPaths <- bind(free = kappa.free, popParam = kappa.pop))
  #------------------------------
  #Endogenous Paths
 
  beta.free <- beta.pop <- matrix(0,
                                  nrow = 1, #each row is an outcome namely Y
                                  ncol = 1, #each column is an endogenous predictor Y
                                  dimnames = list(c("Y","Y"),
                                                  c("Y", "Y")))
 (endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop))
 
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
  #We will also calculate power for certain indirect effects of interest
  userParams <- '
 
          Ind.Effect.Prof := a.Prof*b1.Comp
          Ind.Effect.ManComp := a.ManComp*b1.Comp
          Ind.Effect.Inter := a.Inter*b1.Comp

          '
 
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
  residCor <- binds(free = diag(as.numeric(NA), 1), popParam = diag(1))
 
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
  #Assemble the model
  simMod1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor,
                        KA = exoPaths,
                        indLab = rownames(kappa.free),
                        covLab = colnames(kappa.free), con = userParams)
  set.seed(123)
  datmod <- generate(simMod1, covData = exodata, n = nrow(exodata), type="bootstrap")

  fit1 <- analyze(simMod1, data = datmod)
  summary(fit1)
 
#function to take MC intervals
 rejectMCCI <- function(object) {
    CIs <- semTools::monteCarloCI(object)
    apply(CIs, MARGIN = 1, function(CI) 0 < CI["ci.lower"] | 0 > CI["ci.upper"])
  }
  rejectMCCI(fit1)
 
 sim1 <- sim(nRep = 100, model = fit1, covData = exodata, n = nrow(exodata),
              meanstructure = FALSE, # pass this argument to lavaan
              # parallel processing can reduce computation time:
              multicore = TRUE, numProc = parallel::detectCores() - 1L,
              silent = TRUE, seed = 123, outfun = rejectMCCI)
  summaryParam(sim1, matchParam = TRUE, digits = 3)
  testMCCI <- do.call(rbind, getExtraOutput(sim1))
  testMCCI_df<-as.data.frame(testMCCI)
  nrow(testMCCI_df)
###############################################################

Code 2
 
Then, I tried to use another simpler way, which I studied in an old tutorial. However, the problem with this method was that I could not start X with 0 and 1 and estimate MC intervals.

 sample <- 100
  population.model<-'y ~ 0.2*x1'
  analysis.model <- ' y ~ x1 '
   
 sim1 <- sim(nRep = 100, model=analysis.model,
                      n =  sample , generate=pop.model,
                      lavaanfun = "sem", seed=123, multicore=TRUE)
The latter code provided power but not with the CI i wanted and not with X distribution I needed.

Do you know which approach is correct and how I can improve it?

Thank you in advance, and sorry if the answer is pretty simple (I am just not very familiar with the tools) :)

John
